segmentation.text: When official traffic-control devices are not in place or not in operation,
the driver of a vehicle
shall yield the right-of-way,
slowing down or stopping if need be so to yield,
to a pedestrian crossing the highway within a crosswalk
when the pedestrian is upon the half of the highway upon which the vehicle is traveling or onto which the vehicle is turning,
or when the pedestrian is approaching so closely from the opposite half of the highway as to be in danger.

As used in this section, “half of the highway” means all traffic lanes of a highway which are designated for traffic traveling in one direction, and includes the entire highway in the case of a one-way highway.

elements.justification: The official traffic-control devices (DEF-NRS-484A-145: every 'sign, signal, marking and device ... for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic') that regulate a crosswalk crossing are the vehicular signal heads (dev.traffic_signal, state including 'dark') and pedestrian heads (dev.pedestrian_signal, state including 'dark') that control the travel regions the vehicle and the pedestrian are in: dev.governs ('the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'), with rel.occupies anchoring each road user in a governed region (kind st.travel_region). 'not in operation' is a head showing 'dark' or dev.inoperative ('a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication'); 'not in place' is no such head governing those regions. dev.governs is used for control, not for a position, as its exclusion requires.

'the driver of a vehicle' maps, as in the run's index, to the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', with its exceptions decided by the reading); 'driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080) is a role, read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

Yielding the right-of-way (DEF-NRS-484A-210: 'the right of one vehicle or pedestrian to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another') is observed as the vehicle not reaching the pedestrian: no rel.contact ('the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap') and the vehicle's speed (kin.speed) bounded as the standard below sets; as mapped in the run's index for 'shall yield the right-of-way'.

'a pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian. 'crossing the highway within a crosswalk': the crosswalk (DEF-NRS-484A-065: 'That part of a highway at an intersection included within the connections of the lateral lines of the sidewalks ... or (2) Any portion of a highway ... distinctly indicated for pedestrian crossing') is st.crosswalk ('marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection'), marked or unmarked, so the definition's whole extent is kept; rel.occupies places the pedestrian's footprint in it.

By the section's own definition, a half of the highway is 'all traffic lanes ... designated for traffic traveling in one direction': the pedestrian's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a lane (st.lane) or a one-way roadway (st.one_way_roadway, 'the entire highway in the case of a one-way highway') whose designated direction (st.lane_direction, 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in') points with the vehicle's heading (kin.heading, 'direction the body points'): the half on which the vehicle travels, or, while it turns, the half its heading has turned onto. kin.heading is read as the direction of travel of a vehicle driven forward; st.lane 'Not a stand-in for' a half of the roadway does not apply because the half is assembled from the lanes' designated directions, as the definition itself builds it.

The section's definition of 'half of the highway' ('all traffic lanes of a highway which are designated for traffic traveling in one direction', 'the entire highway in the case of a one-way highway') is carried by the lanes (st.lane) grouped by their designated direction (st.lane_direction) and by a one-way roadway (st.one_way_roadway, 'roadway on which traffic is restricted to one direction'), the atoms c3 and st2 read.

operationalizations.standard: slowing down or stopping if need be so to yield (the right-of-way's 'danger of a crash unless one grants precedence')
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: while the vehicle moves (speed above the halt tolerance), a predicted closest approach of the two centres within the conflict horizon at a centre distance below the conflict clearance is a danger of a crash the driver has not yielded to; a vehicle at rest has slowed or stopped as need be

operationalizations.standard: approaching so closely from the opposite half as to be in danger
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: a pedestrian in the crosswalk on a lane whose designated direction points against the vehicle's heading is in danger where the predicted closest approach of the two centres falls within the conflict horizon at a centre distance below the conflict clearance

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), not engaged by LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1, LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2, LVMC_11_46_030_o1 or LVMC_11_46_030_o2. Devices are not in place or not in operation: every traffic signal head (dev.traffic_signal) that governs (dev.governs) a travel region the subject occupies shows dark or is inoperative (dev.inoperative). There is a pedestrian p (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) whose footprint overlaps a crosswalk (st.crosswalk), such that every pedestrian signal head governing a travel region p occupies shows dark, p is not engaged by NRS_484B_287_1c, NRS_484B_287_1d, NRS_484B_287_1e, LVMC_11_30_060_A or LVMC_11_30_060_B, and either (a) p's footprint overlaps a lane or one-way roadway whose designated direction (st.lane_direction) has a positive dot product with the subject's heading (kin.heading) — the subject's half — or (b) otherwise (p on the opposite half) the predicted closest approach of the subject and p falls within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).
obligation: For every such pedestrian p: the subject is not in contact with p (rel.contact), and where the subject's speed (kin.speed) is above p.halt_speed_tolerance, it is not the case that the closest approach of the subject and p falls within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.
'official' is read through the presence of the signal heads in the scene.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: No signal head governs the subject's lane; a pedestrian stands in an unmarked crosswalk on a lane whose direction matches the subject's heading, 15 m ahead; the subject moves at 10 m/s with a predicted closest approach of 0.5 m in 1.5 s.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene, but the subject is at rest (speed 0.0 m/s) before the crosswalk while the pedestrian crosses its half.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A traffic signal head governing the subject's lane shows circular_green: the devices are in operation.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: No signal head governs the subject's lane; a pedestrian near the crosswalk is on the predicted collision course, but whether its footprint overlaps the crosswalk is not observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: No signal heads and no pedestrian anywhere in the scene: the duty is decided for the subject alone as not engaged.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian in the crosswalk on the opposite half, on a lane whose direction points against the subject's heading, with no predicted closest approach within the horizon.

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: traffic-conflict technique literature (Hayward 1972; Swedish traffic conflict technique)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book passenger-car design vehicle dimensions

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard's kinematic channel

segmentation.text: A pedestrian
shall not suddenly leave a curb or other place of safety and walk or run into the path of a vehicle
which is so close that it is impossible for the driver to yield.

elements.justification: 'A pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair ...').

Leaving 'a curb or other place of safety' is the pedestrian's footprint (rel.occupies) coming onto the roadway (st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic') from a place pedestrians are safe from vehicles: the sidewalk the curb bounds (st.sidewalk, 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line'), a safety zone (st.safety_zone, 'an area within the highway marked off for pedestrians only') or a median or dividing section (st.median_or_divider). st.sidewalk is not used for a crosswalk, as its exclusion requires; st.roadway is not used for the sidewalk. 'into the path of a vehicle': the vehicle is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; the pedestrian is in its path where, under constant velocities, the two centres approach within the conflict horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below the conflict clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance). These primitives are 'Not a stand-in for' contact or danger alone; here they bound the path the vehicle will sweep, the clearance and horizon set by the reading, and the impossibility is decided by the standard.

operationalizations.standard: so close that it is impossible for the driver to yield
operationalizations.convention: stopping-distance model: the vehicle cannot yield where the time to the predicted closest approach (prim.closest_approach_time) is less than the driver's perception-reaction time plus the vehicle's speed (kin.speed) divided by twice the braking deceleration, written as a product (2·a·t_ca < 2·a·t_r + v); the deceleration is selected by the surface: icy or snow-covered (env.ice_or_snow), else wet (env.wet_road), else dry

applicability: The subject is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) that leaves a place of safety at this observation: its footprint overlaps a roadway (st.roadway) here, and at the previous observation it overlapped no roadway and overlapped a sidewalk, a safety zone or a median or divider. The duty does not apply where NRS_484B_287_1c, NRS_484B_287_1d, NRS_484B_287_1e, LVMC_11_30_060_A, LVMC_11_30_060_B, LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1 or LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2 is engaged for the subject, nor where LVMC_11_46_030_o1 or LVMC_11_46_030_o2 is engaged for a vehicle v of the scene.
obligation: There is no vehicle v (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) such that the closest approach of the subject and v falls within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance) and 2·a·t < 2·a·p.driver_reaction_time + speed(v), where t is prim.closest_approach_time with horizon p.conflict_horizon, speed(v) is v's kin.speed, and a is p.following_decel_ice where env.ice_or_snow holds, else p.following_decel_wet where env.wet_road holds, else p.following_decel_dry. With no vehicle in the scene, compliant.

narrowings.why: 'suddenly' is read through the vehicle's closeness at the moment the pedestrian leaves the place of safety: a departure is sudden in the law's sense where the vehicle is already too close to yield; the pedestrian's own abruptness is not measured.
'other place of safety' is read only through the sidewalk the curb bounds, a safety zone and a median or dividing section.
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's motion: whether the vehicle can stop, whoever or whatever controls it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Dry road. The pedestrian steps from the sidewalk onto the roadway while a car 12 m away moves toward it at 12 m/s; predicted closest approach 0.5 m in 1.0 s, below 1.5 s + 12/(2·6) s.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian stays on the sidewalk throughout.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car is 12 m away at 12 m/s on a collision course, but whether the pedestrian's footprint overlaps the roadway or the sidewalk is not observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian steps off the sidewalk with no vehicle in the scene: the duty binds the pedestrian alone and is met.

segmentation.text: Whenever signals exhibiting the words “Walk,” “Don’t Walk,” “Wait” or similar symbols are in place, such signals indicate as follows:
While the “Walk” indication or walking person symbol is illuminated,
pedestrians facing the signal
may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal
and must be given
the right-of-way
by the drivers of all vehicles.

elements.justification: Signals exhibiting 'Walk', 'Don't Walk', 'Wait' or similar symbols are pedestrian heads (dev.pedestrian_signal: 'a pedestrian head; state ∈ {walk, dont_walk_flashing, dont_walk_steady, dark}'); 'in place' is a head present in the scene. 'such signals' regulate the crossing of the roadway they control: dev.governs ('the travel regions whose traffic the device controls — a lane, ... roadway'), traffic including pedestrians (DEF-NRS-484A-285: 'pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles'), ties the head to the roadway or lane its crossing traverses (kinds st.roadway, st.lane). dev.governs is not used as a position.
'the “Walk” indication or walking person symbol is illuminated' is the head's state walk (dev.pedestrian_signal state 'walk').

'pedestrians' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian. 'facing the signal': the head's location (dev.position, 'location of the device head / sign face') lies ahead of the pedestrian's position (kin.position) along the direction its body points (kin.heading, 'direction the body points'), within a cone and a reach. dev.position is used as the head's location, not as the place of a stop line or crossing, which its exclusion names.

'may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal' identifies the pedestrians the right-of-way is owed to: those on the roadway the head governs (rel.occupies of a st.roadway or st.lane region that head governs), facing the head, so moving toward it across the way. The highway (DEF-NRS-484A-095: 'the entire width between the boundary lines') is crossed by traversing its roadway; the sidewalk the words of the sibling subparagraphs call a place of safety is no part of the crossing.

Giving the right-of-way (DEF-NRS-484A-210: 'the right of one vehicle or pedestrian to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another') is observed as the vehicle not reaching the pedestrian (no rel.contact) with its speed (kin.speed) bounded as the standard sets, as the index maps 'Yield'.
'the drivers of all vehicles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, the driver read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: precedence where the two approach 'under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence' (DEF-NRS-484A-210)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: while the vehicle moves (speed above the halt tolerance), a predicted closest approach of the two centres within the conflict horizon at a centre distance below the conflict clearance is a danger of a crash in which the vehicle has not granted precedence

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), not engaged by LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1, LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2, LVMC_11_46_030_o1 or LVMC_11_46_030_o2. There are a pedestrian p (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian), a pedestrian signal head d showing walk, and a roadway or lane r governed by d (dev.governs), with p's footprint overlapping r (rel.occupies), p facing d, and p not engaged by NRS_484B_287_1c, NRS_484B_287_1d, NRS_484B_287_1e, LVMC_11_30_060_A or LVMC_11_30_060_B. p faces d where, with Δ the vector from p's kin.position to d's dev.position and h p's kin.heading: h·Δ > 0, (h·Δ)² ≥ p.ped_signal_facing_cos² · (Δx² + Δy²), and Δx² + Δy² ≤ p.ped_signal_facing_reach².
obligation: For every such pedestrian p: the subject is not in contact with p (rel.contact), and where the subject's speed (kin.speed) is above p.halt_speed_tolerance, it is not the case that the closest approach of the subject and p falls within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).

narrowings.why: 'the drivers' is read through the vehicles' controlled motion: the duty binds each vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian on the roadway faces a pedestrian head 12 m ahead that governs that roadway and shows walk; the subject turns toward the crossing at 8 m/s with a predicted closest approach of 0.8 m in 1.2 s.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene with the subject at rest before the crossing.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The faced head shows dont_walk_steady.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Same as forbid, but the head's state is not observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The head shows walk but no pedestrian is in the scene: decided for the subject alone as not engaged.

param_proposals.source: traffic-conflict technique literature (Hayward 1972; Swedish traffic conflict technique)

param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book passenger-car design vehicle dimensions

segmentation.text: Whenever signals exhibiting the words “Walk,” “Don’t Walk,” “Wait” or similar symbols are in place, such signals indicate as follows:
While the “Don’t Walk” or “Wait” indication or an upraised hand symbol is illuminated, is flashing and is accompanied by a countdown timer,
a pedestrian
may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal,
but must complete the crossing before the countdown timer gets to zero.

elements.justification: Signals exhibiting 'Walk', 'Don't Walk', 'Wait' or similar symbols are pedestrian heads (dev.pedestrian_signal: 'a pedestrian head; state ∈ {walk, dont_walk_flashing, dont_walk_steady, dark}; countdown attribute when a timer is displayed'); 'such signals' regulate the crossing of the roadway they control, read through dev.governs ('the travel regions whose traffic the device controls — a lane, ... roadway'; traffic includes pedestrians, DEF-NRS-484A-285) on a roadway or lane (kinds st.roadway, st.lane).

'“Don’t Walk” or “Wait” indication or an upraised hand symbol is illuminated, is flashing and is accompanied by a countdown timer' is the head's state dont_walk_flashing with its countdown attribute displayed.
'a pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian.

The pedestrian who proceeds across the highway under this indication is one whose footprint came onto the governed roadway or lane (rel.occupies of st.roadway / st.lane) while the head showed it, facing the head: the head's location (dev.position, 'location of the device head') ahead of the pedestrian's position (kin.position) along its heading (kin.heading, 'direction the body points') within a cone and a reach — the direction of the signal. dev.position is not used as a crossing or a stop line.

Completing the crossing is having left the roadway or lane crossed: the pedestrian's footprint no longer overlaps it (rel.occupies). The countdown timer gets to zero at the end of the flashing interval it times, where the head stops showing the flashing indication with a countdown and shows dont_walk_steady (dev.pedestrian_signal states dont_walk_flashing with countdown, then dont_walk_steady).

applicability: The subject is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian), not engaged by NRS_484B_287_1c, NRS_484B_287_1d, NRS_484B_287_1e, LVMC_11_30_060_A, LVMC_11_30_060_B, LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1 or LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2, with no vehicle v of the scene engaged by LVMC_11_46_030_o1 or LVMC_11_46_030_o2. The judged observation is the countdown's end for a pedestrian head d governing (dev.governs) a roadway or lane r: d shows dont_walk_steady here and showed dont_walk_flashing with its countdown at the previous observation. The subject's latest entry onto r (the latest earlier observation at which its footprint came to overlap r, not overlapping it at the observation before; history bound: that entry, searched back without other limit) was made while d showed dont_walk_flashing with its countdown and the subject faced d, and d showed dont_walk_flashing with countdown at every observation from that entry to the previous one. The subject faces d where, with Δ the vector from its kin.position to d's dev.position and h its kin.heading: h·Δ > 0, (h·Δ)² ≥ p.ped_signal_facing_cos² · (Δx² + Δy²), and Δx² + Δy² ≤ p.ped_signal_facing_reach². Where the entry lies before the recording, applicability is unknown.
obligation: At the countdown's end the subject's footprint does not overlap r (rel.occupies): it has completed the crossing.

narrowings.why: the countdown's reaching zero is read as the head's change from the flashing indication with countdown to the steady indication, which ends the interval the timer counts; the timer's displayed number is not read.
'complete the crossing' is read as the pedestrian's footprint having left the roadway or lane governed by the head; a pedestrian on a median or safety zone between roadways has left it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The head governing roadway r shows dont_walk_flashing with countdown; the pedestrian steps onto r facing it, walks slowly, and is still on r when the head turns dont_walk_steady.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian steps onto r during the flashing countdown and is on the far sidewalk, off r, when the head turns dont_walk_steady.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian entered r while the head showed walk; at the countdown's end it is still on r (the steady-indication duty governs it, not this one).

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian steps onto r and is on it later, but the head's state is not observed, so neither the countdown interval nor its end can be told.

scenarios.name: history_boundary
scenarios.narrative: The recording begins with the pedestrian already on r while the head shows dont_walk_flashing with countdown; the head turns dont_walk_steady while it is still on r; its entry onto r is not recorded.
scenarios.boundary: the pedestrian's entry onto r, which lies before the recording

segmentation.text: Whenever signals exhibiting the words “Walk,” “Don’t Walk,” “Wait” or similar symbols are in place, such signals indicate as follows:
While the “Don’t Walk” or “Wait” indication or an upraised hand symbol is illuminated and flashing but is not accompanied by a countdown timer,
a pedestrian
may not proceed to cross the highway,
but a pedestrian
who entered the highway lawfully pursuant to subparagraph (1)
may continue to cross the highway
but must proceed to a curb, sidewalk, safety zone if one is provided or other place of safety before the “Don’t Walk” or “Wait” indication or an upraised hand symbol is illuminated and steady.

elements.justification: Signals exhibiting 'Walk', 'Don't Walk', 'Wait' or similar symbols are pedestrian heads (dev.pedestrian_signal: 'a pedestrian head; state ∈ {walk, dont_walk_flashing, dont_walk_steady, dark}; countdown attribute'). The signal that indicates to a pedestrian ('such signals') is the head that governs the roadway or lane its crossing traverses (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls', traffic including pedestrians by DEF-NRS-484A-285; kinds st.roadway, st.lane) and that the pedestrian faces: the head's location (dev.position, 'location of the device head') ahead of the pedestrian's position (kin.position) along its heading (kin.heading, 'direction the body points') within a cone and a reach. dev.position is not used as a stop line or crossing.
'illuminated and flashing but is not accompanied by a countdown timer' is the head's state dont_walk_flashing with no countdown attribute displayed.
'a pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian.

Proceeding to cross the highway is coming onto the roadway or lane the head governs: the pedestrian's footprint comes to overlap it (rel.occupies of st.roadway / st.lane). The highway (DEF-NRS-484A-095) includes the sidewalk, but the sibling words 'must proceed to a curb, sidewalk, safety zone' place the sidewalk outside the crossing, so the crossing begins on the roadway.
'a pedestrian' (the one excepted) is the same admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian.

Entering the highway lawfully pursuant to subparagraph (1) borrows (1)'s words: 'While the “Walk” indication or walking person symbol is illuminated, pedestrians facing the signal may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal'. It is the pedestrian's latest step from a sidewalk (st.sidewalk) onto a roadway or lane (rel.occupies of st.roadway / st.lane) made while a pedestrian head (dev.pedestrian_signal) governing that roadway or lane (dev.governs) showed walk and the pedestrian faced it (dev.position ahead of kin.position along kin.heading within the cone and reach).
Continuing to cross is not having returned to a sidewalk (rel.occupies of st.sidewalk) since that entry: the pedestrian is still in the crossing it began.

'After complying with the requirement to stop' requires the halt itself (rule 5), with every qualification of the requirement it names, borrowed from NRS-484B-307-8a (reference s3): 'must stop before entering the crosswalk on the nearest side of the intersection where the sign or pavement marking indicates where the stop must be made, or in the absence of any such crosswalk, sign or marking, then before entering the intersection'. A stop required is DEF-NRS-484A-255, 'complete cessation from movement': drv.motion.complete_halt. The place: the stop line (st.stop_line, 'the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device') recorded as marking the entrance of the rider's carrier c (st.entrance_of), else the crosswalk (st.crosswalk) marking it, else c's entrance end at the intersection (st.intersection); the footprint not overlapping the region (rel.occupies), on its upstream side along c's designated direction (st.lane_direction, sign of prim.region_offset_along) and within p.stop_point_tolerance of it (st.region_geometry distance), on the approach that ends in this entry, as NRS_484B_307_8a_o1 states the place, zone and history bound. The admitted aggregates for the defined words: DEF-NRS-484A-135::motorcycle ('every motor vehicle equipped with a seat or saddle for the use of the driver and designed to travel on not more than three wheels'), DEF-NRS-484A-125::moped ('a motor-driven scooter, motor-driven cycle or similar vehicle that is propelled by a small engine'), DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle ('a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride'), DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle and DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter, claimed as ru.aggregate and never expanded. Same words, same atoms as the index (NRS_484B_307_2a).

'the applicable official traffic-control device': the signal installation of the intersection the rider is at, observed through its heads: the traffic signal heads (dev.traffic_signal) that govern (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') a travel region (st.travel_region) entering i (st.lane_enters; st.intersection); the head s governing c is the rider's own. 'official' (DEF-NRS-484A-145, 'placed or erected by a public authority') is presumed from the head's presence (narrowing). 'waits for two complete cycles of the lights or lighted arrows': from the latest onset of its halt at the place until its entry into i the rider does not overlap i, and in that interval some head of the installation begins a green indication (circular_green or a green_arrow, the lights or lighted arrows that come on once in each cycle of the installation) at least two times: a count of that head's rising green indications since the halt's onset, against the literal two. These are the nearest atoms only: the count's bound, the figure two the law states, cannot be written as a literal the formula carries (gap on this span).
'the signal does not change': the rider's head s (dev.traffic_signal) displays the steady red alone (circular_red, no other state) at every observation from the latest onset of the halt to the entry.

'No other device at the place prohibits': a regulatory sign (dev.regulatory_sign, 'a point regulation by catalogue code', codes no_left_turn and no_right_turn) governing (dev.governs) the rider's carrier c (st.travel_region) or the intersection i (st.intersection). Not a stand-in: 'a prohibition sign is a condition', and it is read as one, not as a manoeuvre. 'official' status is presumed from presence.

'either or both such turns, if applicable': the turn the rider makes on this passage through intersection i (st.intersection), from its entry (rel.occupies rising) to its exit, recognized at the exit as a right turn (drv.motion.right_turn_through_region, 'a turn to the right through region r, recognized as it leaves r') or a left turn (drv.motion.left_turn_through_region); 'if applicable': only a turn made brings a prohibition into play, and a straight passage is never prohibited by a turn sign. Read from each observation of the passage at the recognition the passage reaches, so that the condition is decided at the entry where the exit is recorded.

'yields': kin.speed ('magnitude of velocity') tells a rider that moves on toward the other road user from one that holds back, and rel.contact ('the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)') is the crash precedence exists to avoid; not a stand-in for a near miss, which the operationalization of s14 reads. As the index maps 'must yield' (NRS_484B_307_2a).

'pedestrians and other traffic': road users of the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian and DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic other than the rider. 'proceeding': moving, kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance. 'as directed by the signal at the intersection': it overlaps (rel.occupies) intersection i (st.intersection) or a crosswalk (st.crosswalk) recorded as marking the entrance (st.entrance_of) of a travel region that enters i (st.lane_enters, st.travel_region), or it occupies a travel region c' entering i that is governed (dev.governs) by a head displaying a green indication (dev.traffic_signal: circular_green or green_arrow). Not a stand-in: st.entrance_of is the recorded association, never a distance.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: DEF-NRS-484A-210, 'the right of one vehicle or pedestrian to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another vehicle or pedestrian approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence to the other'
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: the danger of a crash is a closest approach of the two centres, under constant velocities, within the time-to-collision horizon (p.conflict_horizon) at a centre distance below the conflict clearance (p.conflict_centre_clearance); the rider grants precedence where, while its speed is above the halt tolerance (p.halt_speed_tolerance), no such approach to the other road user arises. Direction, speed and proximity enter by degree through the constant-velocity extrapolation of both road users.

compositions.quote: must stop before entering the crosswalk on the nearest side of the intersection where the sign or pavement marking indicates where the stop must be made, or in the absence of any such crosswalk, sign or marking, then before entering the intersection
compositions.why: The words borrow the requirement's place and its order (the crosswalk on the nearest side, or the place a sign or pavement marking indicates, else the intersection's edge) and the meaning of stopping before it. The condition requires that the halt itself occurred there; a composition with NRS_484B_307_8a_o1 would not establish it, since a composed rule counts as complied with where it is not engaged, and this paragraph governs riders whether or not that duty engages them (a bicycle or electric scooter is no vehicle). So the borrowed words are carried by the halt, the place and the approach on s2, and no rule of NRS-484B-307-8a need apply, hold or be complied with.

residues.why: The words give the cause of the unchanged red. A head that keeps its steady red alone through two complete cycles of the installation's other indications while the rider waits at its stop place has not served the rider's approach, which is a malfunction or a failure to detect the rider; the duty is the same whichever of the two causes holds, and neither shows in the scene beyond the unchanged red (s8) and the cycles (s7), which the rule reads.

applicability: The subject is of one of the classes motorcycle, moped, bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter (admitted aggregates) or a ru.motorcycle (the trimobile). It approached intersection i through a travel region c whose entrance end is i (st.lane_enters) and which a traffic signal head s governs (dev.governs), and halted (drv.motion.complete_halt, p.halt_speed_tolerance) at the place of the stop on that approach: the stop line recorded as marking c's entrance, else the crosswalk recorded as marking it, else c's entrance end at i, with the zone (p.stop_point_tolerance) and the history bound NRS_484B_307_8a_o1 states. From the latest onset of that halt until its entry into i, s displayed a steady red alone (circular_red, no other state) at every observation and the subject's footprint did not overlap i; in that interval some traffic signal head governing a travel region that enters i began a green indication (circular_green or a green_arrow rising) at least two times (literal 2). The subject then entered i (its footprint came to overlap i, having occupied c at the observation before) while s still displayed the steady red alone, and its footprint has overlapped i at every observation since that entry, the judged one included. It is not the case that the passage through i begun at that entry is recognized at its exit (at the judged observation or a later one: the observation at which the subject's footprint ceases to overlap i) as a right turn (drv.motion.right_turn_through_region; step = p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph, turn_min = p.turn_heading_min, u_turn_min = p.u_turn_heading_min) while a regulatory sign coded no_right_turn governs c or i, nor as a left turn (drv.motion.left_turn_through_region) while one coded no_left_turn governs c or i; where no such sign governs, this condition holds whatever the movement, and where one governs and the exit is not recorded, it is unknown.
obligation: For every road user p other than the subject that is of the class pedestrian or of the class traffic and is proceeding as directed by the signal at i — its speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance, and either its footprint overlaps i or a crosswalk recorded as marking the entrance of a travel region that enters i, or it occupies a travel region c' entering i governed by a head that displays circular_green or a green_arrow: it is not the case that the subject's speed is above p.halt_speed_tolerance while the closest approach of the two centres lies within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance); and the subject's body does not touch p's (rel.contact).

narrowings.why: 'driving' and 'riding' are read through the road user's controlled motion, whoever or whatever is at its controls.
'official' traffic-control device: the presence of the signal heads at the intersection is the evidence of their official status.

'proceeding as directed by the signal at the intersection' is read through the signal state governing the other road user's approach (a green indication) where it approaches, and through its presence within the intersection or an adjacent crosswalk where it is there; a road user that entered against its own red and is now within the intersection is yielded to as well.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A moped halts 1 m short of the stop line marking lane c's entrance while head s displays circular_red alone; while it waits, the head governing the cross street's lane begins circular_green twice and s stays circular_red alone; no turn-prohibiting sign governs c or i. The moped enters i straight through at 5 m/s while a pedestrian walks at 1.3 m/s in the crosswalk marking the entrance of the far approach, the closest approach of their centres 1.0 s ahead at 0.6 m.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same wait and entry with no other road user in the scene: the duty binds the rider alone and is met.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The moped halts at the line and enters i after the cross street's head has begun circular_green only once since its halt: the wait of two cycles is not met.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the source does not observe which travel regions the heads govern: which head is the rider's and whether the cross head belongs to this intersection are unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the moped halted 15 m short of the line behind a queue and, when the queue cleared, rolled to the line and into i without halting at the place: the halt the requirement to stop names did not occur, and the paragraph does not apply.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but a regulatory sign coded no_right_turn governs lane c and the moped's passage through i is recognized at its exit as a right turn (heading change -85 degrees): a device at the place prohibits the turn it made, and the permission with its yield does not arise.

gaps.proposal: `Formula.countAtLeast` (edge : Formula) (sinceφ : Formula) (n : Term): the count of rising edges of `edge` since `sinceφ` became true (start of its latest run) is at least `n`, where `n` is a constant term in unit count (a Term.lit written through the count unit), so that Formula.literals reports the bound as (n, count) and the gate's literal check reads the figure the law states. Alternatively, Formula.count keeps its form and Formula.literals and the gate's literal collection report its Nat bound as (n, count). It decides the time of the act the law requires before a rider may proceed against a steady red: the wait of two complete cycles of the installation's lights, which separates a lawful proceed after a detector failure from running the red after one cycle. Same distinction as gap G87 filed on NRS-484B-307-9b.
gaps.nearest: Formula.count (edge sinceφ op n) writes the count of the installation's rising green indications since the halt's onset, but its bound n is a bare Nat that Formula.literals does not report: a faithful rule shows formula literals [] against the declared literal (2, count) and the gate returns it BARE_LITERAL. Adding a tautological Term.lit 2 count conjunct, or dropping the figure the law states from the record's literals, is forbidden.

segmentation.text: Where the signal is a steady red signal alone:
Vehicular traffic facing the signal

must stop before entering the crosswalk on the nearest side of the intersection where the sign or pavement marking indicates where the stop must be made, or in the absence of any such crosswalk, sign or marking, then before entering the intersection,
and,
except as otherwise provided in paragraphs (c) and (d) [(c) is appended below, NRS-484B-307-8d],
must remain stopped or standing until the green signal is shown.
After complying with the requirement to stop,
vehicular traffic facing such a signal and situated on the extreme right of the highway
may proceed into the intersection
for a right turn
only when the intersecting highway is two-directional or one-way to the right,
or vehicular traffic facing such a signal and situated on the extreme left of a one-way highway
may proceed into the intersection
for a left turn
only when the intersecting highway is one-way to the left,
but must yield
the right-of-way
to pedestrians and other traffic proceeding as directed by the signal at the intersection.

elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal, 'a signal head; state ∈ {circular_green, circular_yellow, circular_red, ...}; several states may be displayed at once': a steady red signal alone is circular_red and no other state (not flashing_red, and no arrow beside it). Same atom as the index for the signal words of NRS_484B_307_2a.

'Vehicular traffic': the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as ru.aggregate, never expanded. 'facing the signal': the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a travel region c (st.travel_region) whose entrance end is intersection i (st.lane_enters; st.intersection) and which the head governs (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'). Not a stand-in: dev.governs is not a position, st.lane_enters not presence in i. Same words, same atoms as the index (NRS_484B_307_2a).

'remain stopped or standing' (DEF-NRS-484A-255, 'complete cessation from movement'; DEF-NRS-484A-250, 'the halting of a vehicle ... otherwise than for the purpose of and while actually engaged in receiving or discharging passengers') at the place of the stop: the subject's footprint does not come to overlap (rel.occupies) the crosswalk recorded as marking c's entrance (st.crosswalk, st.entrance_of) nor intersection i (st.intersection). 'until the green signal is shown': the duty holds while the head (dev.traffic_signal) displays the steady red alone and ends once it displays another state. Not a stand-in: st.entrance_of is the recorded association, never a distance.

'After complying with the requirement to stop' refers to s3 of this line and requires the halt itself with every qualification s3 states: 'must stop before entering the crosswalk on the nearest side of the intersection where the sign or pavement marking indicates where the stop must be made, or in the absence of any such crosswalk, sign or marking, then before entering the intersection'. A complete halt (drv.motion.complete_halt; DEF-NRS-484A-255, 'complete cessation from movement') at that place — the stop line (st.stop_line) recorded as marking c's entrance (st.entrance_of), else the crosswalk (st.crosswalk) marking it, else c's entrance end at i (st.intersection) — with the footprint not overlapping the region (rel.occupies), on its upstream side along c's direction (st.lane_direction, sign of prim.region_offset_along) and within p.stop_point_tolerance of it (st.region_geometry), on the approach that ends in this entry: the place, zone and history bound of NRS_484B_307_8a_o1. The halt itself, not compliance with that node, which a composed rule grants where it is not engaged. In this node the condition is read where the permission of paragraph (c) takes the subject out of the duty to remain stopped.

'vehicular traffic': the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle. 'facing such a signal': the steady red head governs (dev.governs) the carrier c the subject occupies (rel.occupies), whose entrance end is i (st.lane_enters). 'situated on the extreme right of the highway': c is a lane (st.lane, 'a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles') whose ordinal equals the count of lanes in its direction (st.lane_adjacency, 'lane ordinal within the carriageway and the count of lanes in that direction; ordinal 1 is the leftmost lane'): the rightmost lane. Not a stand-in: lane membership is read from the ordinal, never from a lateral offset.

'may proceed into the intersection': the subject proceeding from the travel region c (st.travel_region) whose entrance end is intersection i (st.lane_enters; st.intersection) toward and into i, its footprint leaving the place of the stop (rel.occupies of the crosswalk marking c's entrance or of i rising); the place at which the intention of s10 is declared. As the index maps 'may proceed into the intersection' (NRS_484B_307_8a_o3).

'the intersecting highway': each highway region (st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines') that i lies on (st.on_way, 'an intersection lies on every way that meets there') other than a highway c lies on. 'two-directional' (DEF-NRS-484B-073, 'an undivided highway upon which vehicles are allowed to proceed in opposite directions'): no median or dividing section (st.median_or_divider, 'physical barrier or dividing section between roadways') lies on it, and two lanes (st.lane) lying on it carry designated directions (st.lane_direction) whose cosine is below minus p.lane_opposed_direction_cos. 'one-way to the right': at least one lane lies on it and every lane lying on it carries a designated direction to the right of c's designated direction, the cross product of c's direction with the lane's (d_x times l_y minus d_y times l_x) being below minus p.cross_direction_sin_min. Not a stand-in: st.on_way is the way a region lies on, not nearness; st.lane_direction is local to its carrier.

'vehicular traffic facing such a signal': as s8. 'situated on the extreme left': c is a lane (st.lane) of ordinal 1 (st.lane_adjacency, 'ordinal 1 is the leftmost lane'); 'of a one-way highway': the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a one-way roadway (st.one_way_roadway, 'roadway on which traffic is restricted to one direction'), as the index maps 'Upon a highway designated and signposted for one-way traffic' (NRS_484B_220_1). Not a stand-in: lane membership is read from the ordinal, never from an offset.
As s9: the subject proceeding from c into i (rel.occupies rising; st.lane_enters; st.travel_region; st.intersection), the place at which the intention of s14 is declared.

'the intersecting highway': each highway region (st.highway) that i lies on (st.on_way) other than a highway c lies on. 'one-way to the left': at least one lane (st.lane) lies on it and every lane lying on it carries a designated direction (st.lane_direction) to the left of c's designated direction, the cross product of c's direction with the lane's being above p.cross_direction_sin_min. Not a stand-in: st.on_way is not nearness.

applicability: The subject, of the classes traffic and vehicle, occupies at the judged observation, or occupied at the previous one, a travel region c whose entrance end is intersection i (st.lane_enters) and which a traffic signal head s governs (dev.governs); s displays a steady red alone (circular_red, no other state) at the judged observation; and at the previous observation the subject's footprint overlapped neither i nor a crosswalk recorded as marking c's entrance (st.entrance_of). The duty does not apply where paragraph (c) permits the movement (spans s7 to s15, the words NRS_484B_307_8a_o3 reads as its conditions): the subject has halted at the place of the stop on this approach (drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance; the place, zone p.stop_point_tolerance and history bound of NRS_484B_307_8a_o1: the search runs back from the judged observation to the approach start on c or to the subject's previous entry into i from c), and either (right) c is a lane whose ordinal equals the count of lanes in its direction, int.right_turn is declared true for the subject at i, and every highway i lies on other than one c lies on is two-directional (no median or divider lies on it; two lanes on it with directions opposed within p.lane_opposed_direction_cos) or one-way to the right (every lane on it points to the right of c's direction by more than p.cross_direction_sin_min); or (left) c is a lane of ordinal 1, the subject's footprint overlaps a one-way roadway, int.left_turn is declared true for the subject at i, and every such highway is one-way to the left. The permission is read whether the subject's footprint now overlaps the crosswalk marking c's entrance or i itself. The duty also does not apply where NRS_484B_307_8d (paragraph (d), s5) applies to the subject.
obligation: At the judged observation the subject's footprint overlaps neither i nor a crosswalk recorded as marking c's entrance (rel.occupies): having stopped, or still short of the place, it remains short of them while the steady red alone is displayed; once s displays another state (the green shown) the duty no longer applies.

narrowings.why: 'remain stopped or standing' is read at the place the stop was due: the subject leaves the stop when its footprint comes to overlap the crosswalk marking its carrier's entrance or the intersection while the steady red alone is displayed. A movement short of them, such as closing up behind a vehicle ahead before reaching the place or a creep within the stop-point zone, is not read as leaving the stop: the stop the words require is the one at the place.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car halts at the stop line of lane c (ordinal 2 of 3), which enters i and is governed by head s displaying circular_red alone; int.right_turn is not declared; 5 s later it moves off and its footprint comes to overlap the crosswalk marking c's entrance while s still displays circular_red alone.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The car halts at the line under circular_red alone and stays short of the crosswalk until s displays circular_green; it then enters i.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: s displays circular_green alone throughout the car's approach and entry.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the source does not observe which travel regions s governs: whether the car faces s is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The car halts with its body 1 m short of the stop line in the rightmost lane (ordinal 3 of 3), int.right_turn is declared for it at i, and the cross street is undivided with lanes in both directions; it moves off and its footprint comes to overlap the crosswalk marking c's entrance under circular_red alone: paragraph (c)'s permission holds.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As branch_1, but the cross street is one-way and every lane on it points to the car's left: the permission does not hold, and leaving the stop under the red violates.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: As branch_1, but the car halted 15 m short of the line behind a queue and, when the queue cleared, rolled to the line and into the crosswalk without halting at the place: the halt the permission refers to did not occur.

param_proposals.convention: the body-to-mark gap within which a halt counts as at the mark: a stop line's set-back before a crossing plus a placement margin

param_proposals.name: p.lane_opposed_direction_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest angle (about twenty-five degrees) off exactly opposed at which the designated directions of two mapped lanes of one way count as opposite directions of travel: the direction noise of map lane segments along a gently curving way
